broker.name: Moneta Markets
broker.tagline: Its site names 5 regulators, including FSCA, FCA, and CMA. Rules depend on where you live. Advertised leverage: Up to 1:1000.
broker.about: The Moneta Markets pages checked on 11 October 2026 do not state a founding year or one headquarters. Account names on its site include Direct STP, Prime ECN, and Ultra ECN. Platforms named there include PRO Trader, MetaTrader 4, MetaTrader 5, AppTrader, and TradingView. The site names these regulators: FSCA, FCA, CMA, FSC (Mauritius), and SLIBC. The company on an account depends on where the client lives. Minimum deposit is not a single number on the pages that loaded. The highest leverage figure taken from those pages is Up to 1:1000. Leverage increases losses as well as gains.
broker.regulators_note: The company behind an account depends on where you live. FSCA: Moneta Markets South Africa (Pty) Ltd, 47490. FCA: Moneta Markets Capital Ltd, 613381. CMA: Moneta Global Financial Services L.L.C, 20200000459. FSC (Mauritius): Moneta Markets Trading Limited, GB24203391. SLIBC: Moneta Markets Ltd, 2023-00068.

broker.costs_note: Spreads and commissions move with the market, and they are not the same at every company in the group.

leverage.note: English leverage page also says clients can choose from 100:1 up to 1000:1 on FX.

broker.leverage_note: Leverage increases losses as well as gains, and you can lose more than you deposit. The highest figure on this card is the highest number this broker advertises. It is not the cap on every account. The cap depends on the company, the product and where you live.

other_fees.label: Minimum deposit
other_fees.note: Varies by account and payment method. English FAQ: deposits from $50 by bank wire and credit/debit card, a live account can be kept at a $0 balance, and some methods have a higher minimum. The same FAQ says the minimum deposit is $50 depending on account type. The Portuguese compare page shows $50 for Direct STP and Prime ECN, and $20,000 for Ultra ECN.

other_fees.label: Deposits and withdrawals
other_fees.note: English FAQ. Overseas banks may charge intermediary fees. Minimum withdrawal is $40 USD or the equivalent. The FAQ also says Moneta Markets will cover a $20 USD bank/wire fee charged by the client's institution for one deposit each month.

other_fees.label: Trading costs
other_fees.value: spreads and swaps; a small index fee per lot
other_fees.note: FAQ: costs from spreads and swap fees. Indices incur a small fee per lot by the liquidity provider. No other handling fees are charged, on that FAQ answer.
